# Nāgārjuna — Fundamental Wisdom of the Middle Way (Garfield, 1995)

[Source index](../../../README.md) · [Reading entrance](../../../../../../README.md) · [48 movements](../../../../../../section-rooms/README.md)

## Bibliographic identity

Oxford University Press identifies Jay L. Garfield's 1995 translation and commentary on Nāgārjuna's *Mūlamadhyamakakārikā* as the selected edition. It is required as a limiting source against flattening Śaiva *prakāśa*, Buddhist emptiness, and the essay's zero into one doctrine.

## Essay use

### Source's relevant contribution

- A primary-text translation for dependent origination and emptiness, read here chiefly as a limit on metaphysical assimilation.

### Licensed essay use

- Test the essay's zero, relation, and non-duality language against Madhyamaka rather than absorbing it into a generic “Eastern” witness.

### Claim boundary

- Nāgārjuna warrants Madhyamaka arguments within the selected translation and commentary. An enduring self-luminous absolute, QL's sixfold compression, and any AI metaphysics belong to other traditions or to the essay's own derivation; the differences must stay explicit.
